content_preview.title: Gemini CLI 0.64.0 Release Notes List Fixes for Headless Folder-Trust Reporting, Atomic File-Tool Writes and State-File Recovery
content_preview.summary: Gemini CLI v0.64.0, published October 13, lists fixes for folder-trust reporting in headless mode, serialized and atomic file writes, and recovery of its state file from a backup.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Gemini CLI, a terminal coding agent developed in the google-gemini GitHub organization, has a new release. The [v0.64.0 release page](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/releases/tag/v0.64.0) on GitHub was published on October 13, 2026 (20:44 UTC). Its "What's Changed" list is made up largely of fixes. Three of them concern how the agent reports workspace trust, writes files and stores its own state, and each has a pull request whose description explains the change. The desc...

editor_notes.content_quality: Briefing, 667 words (identical raw and with link URLs stripped; within 300-800). Title is 127 characters, under the 150 cap. Clear structure: release entries, then one section per PR, then a limits section. Single-sourced contributor explanations are labelled as the contributors' own account and the article states it is not an independent test.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 snapshots exist (source-0..3.html.gz, HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null for all) and contain real page body, not page chrome only. source-0 (release v0.64.0): contains the full 'What's Changed' list; the page shows 'gemini-cli-robot released this 13 Oct 20:44', datetime attribute 2026-10-13T20:44:46Z, tag commit 4a0749a, labelled 'Latest' (not a pre-release). The live GitHub API re-checked on 2026-10-15 returns published_at 2026-10-13T20:44:46Z, prerelease false, draft false, and releases/latest is v0.64.0, so nothing changed since the snapshot. The three entries appear verbatim: 'fix(cli): propagate resolved folder trust state in headless mode (#29031) by @amelidev in #29528'; 'fix(core): serialize file tool operations and make writes atomic (#29078) by @elberthc-byte in #29499'; 'fix(cli): persist state atomically and recover from backup on corruption by @urielefrenvirtusa in #29558'. The notes contain no prose beyond the list and a Full Changelog link, as the article says. The title phrasing ('Headless Folder-Trust Reporting', 'Atomic File-Tool Writes', 'State-File Recovery') is a fair gloss of those entries, and all three are fix() entries. The article does not state stable or pre-release, so nothing is misstated; the page's 'Latest' label and API prerelease:false are consistent with a stable release. Other entries named (Windows ConPTY IME cursor fix #29560, ACP session fix #29580) are present. source-1 (PR 29528): the Summary confirms useFolderTrust unconditionally reported onTrustChange(true) to AppContainer in headless mode even when isTrusted === false; the phrase 'split-brain state' appears verbatim in the PR author's (amelidev) Summary and the article attributes it to the description; the fix passes true/false/undefined and suppresses isFolderTrustDialogOpen in headless mode. The description does not say what the parent did with the false 'trusted' signal beyond 'AppContainer and its consumers were informed that the folder was trusted', so the article's statement that the practical effect is not described holds. The PR's own matrix covers interactive mode, but the article makes no interactive-versus-headless claim beyond the dialog suppression. Checklist (parsed from checkbox inputs): only 'MacOS npm run' ticked; Windows and Linux unticked. source-2 (PR 29499): withPathLock in-process per-path mutex, EditTool/WriteFileTool serialization, atomic sibling-temp-file rename in StandardFileSystemService.writeTextFile with EBUSY/EPERM/EACCES retries, git snapshot serialization per project root, lost updates / inaccurate diffs / .git/index.lock collisions, manual verification (0 partial reads during a 10MB write; two sub-agents appending both lines preserved): all confirmed. Checklist: only 'Linux npm run' ticked among platforms, Windows unticked. source-3 (PR 29558): ~/.gemini/state.json, temp file + fsync + rename, .bak rotation, .corrupt preservation, fallback to .bak on load, 'interrupted write or crash' example: all confirmed. Checklist: only 'Linux npm run' ticked, Windows unticked. Merge dates (29528 Sep 29, 29499 Sep 30, 29558 Oct 1) pre-date the release; the article gives no merge dates and does not imply the changes are newer than they are. No causal link between the three fixes is asserted. Live re-fetch: the GitHub API release body confirmed the three entries and PR links unchanged. All four sources are GitHub pages with real body content, so no live fallback was needed for any source.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every claim traces to a cited source and is attributed to the release page or to the PR description. Contributor claims are attributed ('the description says', 'the contributor reports'). Freshness: release published 2026-10-13, reviewed 2026-10-15; the publication timestamp is reported correctly. No fabricated specifics found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and descriptive; no editorializing. The limitations paragraph (no user reports, no frequency figures, Windows not ticked despite Windows-specific retry logic) is a factual observation from the checklists, not speculation.
editor_notes.originality: No earlier Gemini CLI release-notes coverage. Earlier Gemini CLI articles (2026-06/01 on the free-user shutdown and Antigravity CLI; 2026-08/14 on Novee security findings) cover different topics and do not conflict; this article only describes the open-source repository's release page and makes no claim about free-tier availability. No internal links in the body.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed Briefing. No suspicious-pattern hits (suspicious_patterns null for all four sources). github.com is already allowlisted, so no allowlist changes. Entry names, quote, timestamp and checklist observations verified against the snapshots and the live GitHub API. APPROVE.
